summary: The root نبع (nbE) primarily refers to a specific tree, known for its strong wood. This wood was commonly used for making shafts, such as those for carts, leading to the term نبعان for the two shafts.
lane: نَبْعٌ ذ The tree so-called: see an ex. of its n. un. in a verse cited voce تَحَوَّفَ and تَخَوَّفَ . -b2- نَبْعٌ : see شَوْحَطٌ and شِرْيَانٌ and فَتْحٌ . -b3- نَبْعَانِ The two shafts of a cart: so called because they were commonly made of wood of the tree called نَبْع : see رَادَّةٌ .

headwords.def: It (water) welled, or issued forth. نَبَعَ عَلَيْهِمْ: see نَبَأَ عليهم.
He (God) made, or caused, water to issue. (Msb.)

The tree so-called: see an ex. of its n. un. in a verse cited voce تَحَوَّفَ and تَخَوَّفَ. نَبْعٌ: see شَوْحَطٌ and شِرْيَانٌ and فَتْحٌ. نَبْعَانِ The two shafts of a cart: so called because they were commonly made of wood of the tree called نَبْع: see رَادَّةٌ.
irregularly formed from the augmented verb أَنْبَعَ: see an ex. in a couplet cited voce سَقَى.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
